# `get_sensor_temperature`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Read the temperature reported by the onboard inertial sensor.

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | method (client sends) |
| Grade | MUTATOR / established (64-bit build; 32-bit build established) |
| Side-effect tier | C |
| Confidence | READ |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.31, handler @0xb6cf0, gsensor_temperature @0x3c71b0 (64-bit build) |

Reads a temperature from the IMU, a sensor chosen by hardware model, and returns it as result.temperature. The name suggests the imaging sensor but the handler reads the inertial sensor; its unit and range are unresolved. Any nonzero helper status, including a missing IMU, is reported as 108 (expected float param), which does not mean a float param was expected.

Side effects: On first use lazily constructs and caches a shared IMU object; construction writes IMU enable, accelerometer and angular-velocity scale and sampling-frequency settings through the sysfs interface. Each call then runs a short subprocess I2C read and refills shared static buffers. Hence tier C although the temperature read itself is a register read. No opened-camera precondition. Every full call also makes the shared diagnostic log writes.

## Request params

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | any | yes | - | Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | Fixed value `"get_sensor_temperature"`. [READ] |
| `params` | any | no | - | Not read. Omission, null, object, scalar and array all take the same path. Clients SHOULD omit it. [READ] |

## Reply

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `jsonrpc` | string | no | - | (error) Added by the socket layer (reply object constructor), not the handler fragment. Normally present; absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply. Receivers MUST NOT require it. Fixed value `"2.0"`. [READ; also OBSERVED on the wire (2026-10-12)] |
| `Timestamp` | string | no | - | (error) Decimal string `<seconds>.<nanoseconds>` with exactly nine fractional digits, formatted with `%ld.%09ld` from clock_gettime clock id 1. Linux clock id 1 is CLOCK_MONOTONIC, so the value is monotonic time, not wall-clock or Unix time (INFERRED from the clock id). On replies it is added by the socket layer and is normally present; receivers MUST NOT require it on replies (absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply). On events it is always written by the event constructor. [READ; wire shape also OBSERVED (2026-10-12)] |
| `method` | string | if the request had an id and a string method (handler errors and 103), except a locally built stop_func relay failure | - | (error) The request method, echoed. Absent on dispatcher errors 100 and 200 and on a stop_func relay failure. [READ] |
| `error` | string | yes | - | (error) Message looked up from the code; unknown codes yield "fail to operate". [READ] |
| `code` | integer | yes | - | (error) Nonzero. A requested code of 0 is coerced to 207. [READ] |
| `id` | any | yes | - | (error) The request id echoed with its JSON type; null on dispatcher errors 100 and 200, where it is the only way to recognise the reply and cannot be matched to a request. [READ] |

## Errors

| Code | Trigger | Label |
|---|---|---|
| 108 | Any nonzero status from the IMU temperature read, including no IMU available | `expected float param` |
| 200 | Dispatcher: request has no id | `invalid id` |
| 100 | Dispatcher: method missing or not a string | `invalid request` |

Bus and subprocess latency, and which IMU model is fitted at run time, are unresolved.

## Example

Request, request:

```json
{"id":33,"method":"get_sensor_temperature"}
```

Reply, ok:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"get_sensor_temperature","result":{"temperature":31.5},"code":0,"id":33}
```

Reply, imu-unavailable:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"get_sensor_temperature","error":"expected float param","code":108,"id":34}
```
